title: Canonical etale/pro-etale exchange comparison for arbitrary discrete rings
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be any discrete commutative ring. Let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$ and $g':X'\to X$ form a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Assume $f$ and $f'$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, meaning that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact and that their diagonals are quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Use the small etale and pro-etale sites and their constant $\Lambda$-module categories [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a corner $T$ put $A_T=\nu_T^*$, the exact derived comparison; write $l_u=u_{\Et}^{-1}$, $r_u=Ru_{\Et,*}$, $p_u=u_{\Proet}^*$ and $s_u=Ru_{\Proet,*}$ on the bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The coefficient identifications on every edge are the canonical pullbacks of the constant ring sheaves.

Let $a_u:A_Ul_u\xrightarrow{\sim}p_uA_V$ be the canonical inverse-image comparison for $u:U\to V$. Let $b_u:A_Vr_u\xrightarrow{\sim}s_uA_U$ for $u=f,f'$ be the canonical direct-image comparison, normalized as the adjoint transpose of $A_U(\varepsilon^e_u)\circ a_{u,r_u}^{-1}$ for the etale counit $\varepsilon^e_u$ [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For $L\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ set
$$S_L=p_g(b_{f,L})\circ a_{g,r_fL}:A_{Y'}l_gr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}p_gs_fA_XL,$$
$$T_L=s_{f'}(a_{g',L})\circ b_{f',l_{g'}L}:A_{Y'}r_{f'}l_{g'}L\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{f'}p_{g'}A_XL.$$
For the etale module exchange $e_L$ of [sk-def-exchange] and precisely the ambient constant-ring pro-etale exchange $e^p_{A_XL}$ of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], both formed as the unit--square--counit mate of the canonical composition comparison, one has
$$T_L\circ A_{Y'}(e_L)=e^p_{A_XL}\circ S_L.$$
The isomorphisms $S_L,T_L$ are natural in $L$. Both pro-etale endpoints $p_gs_fA_XL$ and $s_{f'}p_{g'}A_XL$ are bounded below and classical [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. Neither invertibility of $e_L$ nor properness, torsion, constructibility, finiteness of $\Lambda$, or invertibility of torsion orders is assumed.

source.place: Pro-etale site paragraph: compare the two endpoints and identify the canonical unit--square--counit mate; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change); the coefficient-independent mate-square verification is supplied in the report using the blueprint comparison theorem.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] to each of the four edges for its exact inverse-image comparison, and to f and f' for the direct-image comparisons b_f,b_f'. The latter applications have precisely the required qcqs hypotheses. The theorem allows any discrete commutative ring, and its canonical direct-image transformation is the specified right-derived etale/pro-etale base-change transformation beta of [lem-pe-direct-image-mate-compatibility]. The second identity of that lemma, for u=f and u=f', says that the transpose of beta under p_u dashv s_u is A_U(epsilon^e_u) o a_{u,r_u}^{-1}; since the adjunction correspondence of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is a bijection, beta equals the counit-normalized b_u of the statement. Thus all a_u and these two b_u are natural isomorphisms on the indicated bounded-below categories. In particular the displayed composites S_L and T_L exist and are isomorphisms. Put c_u=a_u^{-1}, and write theta^e:l_{f'}l_g -> l_{g'}l_f and theta^p:p_{f'}p_g -> p_{g'}p_f for the canonical square comparisons. All compositions below are written in the order v o u, meaning first u then v.

source.place: Opening paragraph: inverse-image comparison and the counit-normalized map; qcqs comparison theorem

proof.text:
The composition coherence of [lem-pe-inverse-image-comparison-coherence], with c there equal to our a^{-1}, gives, for every M in D^+(Y_et,Lambda),
 theta^p_{A_Y M} o p_{f'}(a_{g,M}) o a_{f',l_g M}
 = p_{g'}(a_{f,M}) o a_{g',l_f M} o A_{X'}(theta^e_M).  (C)
Indeed, apply its composition equation once to X' -> Y' -> Y and once to X' -> X -> Y. Both composites have the same comparison a_{fg'}=a_{gf'} since fg'=gf'; cancel it and replace the two composition comparisons by their square composite. These are exactly theta^e and theta^p in [sk-def-exchange] and [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], since every coefficient identification is the canonical constant-ring one. The sheaf equations hold termwise on complexes: exactness makes all the functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Their isomorphisms and equations descend uniquely by clauses (2)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], and restrict to D^+. This proves (C) for the specified derived square comparisons, rather than for separately chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Final paragraph: identity and composition coherence and exact passage to complexes

proof.text:
Use [lem-pe-direct-image-mate-compatibility] with u=f and u=f'. Its c is our c_u=a_u^{-1}, its beta is b_u by the normalization fixed in Step 1, and its two direct images are the ordinary derived module direct images. Its counit identity reads
 epsilon^p_{u,A_U N} o p_u(b_{u,N})
 = A_U(epsilon^e_{u,N}) o c_{u,r_u N}.  (E)
Here epsilon^e_u:l_ur_u -> id and epsilon^p_u:p_us_u -> id are the specified counits, and N is any object of D^+(U_et,Lambda). This identity needs no further coefficient or geometric hypothesis. We will use it at N=L for f and at N=l_{g'}L for f'.

source.place: Opening paragraph: compatibility with the adjunction counits

proof.text:
Let F_L=T_L o A_{Y'}(e_L). Under p_{f'} dashv s_{f'} its transpose is epsilon^p_{f',p_{g'}A_X L} o p_{f'}(F_L). Naturality of this counit and the definition of T_L first give
 a_{g',L} o epsilon^p_{f',A_{X'}l_{g'}L} o p_{f'}(b_{f',l_{g'}L}) o p_{f'}A_{Y'}(e_L).
By (E) for f' this equals
 a_{g',L} o A_{X'}(epsilon^e_{f',l_{g'}L}) o c_{f',r_{f'}l_{g'}L} o p_{f'}A_{Y'}(e_L).
Naturality of c_{f'} moves e_L to its left. The transpose formula defining e in [sk-def-exchange] says epsilon^e_{f',l_{g'}L} o l_{f'}(e_L)=l_{g'}(epsilon^e_{f,L}) o theta^e_{r_f L}. Consequently the transpose is exactly
 D_L := a_{g',L} o A_{X'}(l_{g'}(epsilon^e_{f,L})) o A_{X'}(theta^e_{r_f L}) o c_{f',l_g r_f L}.
This is a map p_{f'}A_{Y'}l_g r_f L -> p_{g'}A_X L. The adjunction transpose convention is [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

source.place: Remark 07A7 (remark-base-change): exchange as the transpose of pullback of the counit

proof.text:
Let G_L=e^p_{A_X L} o S_L. By [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], its transpose under p_{f'} dashv s_{f'} is
 p_{g'}(epsilon^p_{f,A_X L}) o theta^p_{s_f A_X L} o p_{f'}p_g(b_{f,L}) o p_{f'}(a_{g,r_f L}).
Naturality of theta^p moves b_f to the left, and (E) for f changes the first two resulting factors to p_{g'}(A_X(epsilon^e_{f,L}) o c_{f,r_f L}). Thus this becomes
 p_{g'}A_X(epsilon^e_{f,L}) o p_{g'}(c_{f,r_f L}) o theta^p_{A_Y r_f L} o p_{f'}(a_{g,r_f L}).
Set M=r_f L in (C), compose on the left with p_{g'}(c_{f,M}) and on the right with c_{f',l_g M}, and cancel a_f with c_f and a_{f'} with c_{f'}. The last three factors then equal a_{g',l_f r_f L} o A_{X'}(theta^e_{r_f L}) o c_{f',l_g r_f L}. Finally naturality of a_{g'} for epsilon^e_{f,L} gives precisely D_L from Step 4. This is the explicit equality of the two transposes.

source.place: Remark 07A7 (remark-base-change); the displayed transpose computation supplies the verification behind Remarks 0E46 and 0E47

proof.text: The adjunction correspondence of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is injective. Since Steps 4-5 give the same transpose D_L for F_L and G_L under the same p_{f'} dashv s_{f'}, they are equal. This is exactly T_L o A_{Y'}(e_L)=e^p_{A_X L} o S_L. The comparisons of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] are natural, and whiskering and composing natural transformations preserves naturality: applying naturality of a_g and b_f successively proves it for S; applying naturality of b_{f'} and a_{g'} proves it for T. All of these equalities are in the ordinary constant-ring module derived categories; no completed or internal condensed-coefficient exchange has been substituted.

source.place: Pro-etale site paragraph: comparisons identify the canonical exchange map

proof.text: For any scheme T and M in D^+(T_et,Lambda), exactness of A_T and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] give H^q(A_T M)=nu_T^*H^q(M) and preserve a lower cohomological bound. Each such sheaf is classical by the module essential-image assertion of [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves]; hence A_T M is a bounded-below classical complex. Now l_g r_f L and r_{f'}l_{g'}L lie in D^+(Y'_et,Lambda) by the domains of [sk-def-exchange]. The isomorphisms S_L and T_L from [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identify the two claimed pro-etale endpoints with A_{Y'} of these two etale complexes. Classicality and boundedness pass across an isomorphism, since its cohomology maps are isomorphisms and the continuity maps defining classicality are natural. This proves both endpoint claims without requiring either exchange map to be invertible.

source.place: Pro-etale site paragraph: comparison of the two endpoints; classicality via the comparison essential image

Source checks: the 'Pro-étale site' paragraph of main-20261015 sk-thm-properbasechange.proof.md (comparisons respect units and counits, so the result is the canonical exchange), and the opening of sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison.proof.md (its map is the adjoint of comparison followed by the étale counit, i.e. the counit-normalized b_u). I also read the last paragraph of lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback.proof.md. No SGA is used. I redid the algebra: (C) follows from the two composition equations of lem-pe-inverse-image-comparison-coherence once c_{gf'}=c_{fg'} is eliminated, and the θ orientations agree with sk-def-exchange and with the ambient θ_□. (E) is exactly the second identity of lem-pe-direct-image-mate-compatibility. The Step 4 and Step 5 transposes both reduce to D_L, and I checked every naturality move and the typing. Step 6 is injectivity of the mate bijection. Step 7 (classicality) holds via exact-functor-bounded-below and the essential-image clause of sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves. Coefficients are ordinary constant Λ for any discrete Λ, and qcqs is required only on f and f'. Small cases checked: f=id, g=id, Λ=0, Λ=Z, L=0. lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange is the same equation for finite Λ only; the item generalizes it, as sk-thm-properbasechange (any commutative Λ) needs, so this is advisory and not a duplicate. One C4 fault, which I fixed: Step 1 credited the comparison theorem's statement with identifying its map as the counit-normalized b_u.
